items.new: First comes white-horse, so called, which is obtained from the tapering part of the fish and also from the thicker portions of his flukes. It is tough with congealed tendons — a wad of muscle — but still contains some oil. After being severed from the whale, the white-horse is first cut into portable oblongs before going to the mincer. They look much like blocks of Berkshire marble.

items.new: But to learn all about these obscure matters, your best course is to go straight down into the blubber-room and have a long talk with its inmates. This place has previously been mentioned as the receptacle for the blanket-pieces when stripped and hoisted from the whale. When the time comes to cut up its contents, this room becomes a scene of terror to all newcomers, especially at night. On one side, lit by a dull lantern, a space has been cleared for the workmen. They generally go in pairs — a pike-and-gaff man and a spademan. The whaling-pike is similar to a frigate's boarding-weapon of the same name. The gaff is something like a boat-hook. With his gaff, the gaffman hooks onto a sheet of blubber and tries to hold it from slipping as the ship pitches and lurches about. Meanwhile, the spademan stands on the sheet itself, chopping it perpendicularly into portable horse-pieces. This spade is as sharp as a whetstone can make it. The spademan's feet are shoeless. The thing he stands on will sometimes irresistibly slide away from him like a sled. If he cuts off one of his own toes, or one of his assistants', would you be very much surprised? Toes are scarce among veteran blubber-room men.

items.new: The try-works are set between the foremast and mainmast, the roomiest part of the deck. The timbers beneath are of unusual strength, fitted to bear the weight of an almost solid mass of brick and mortar, some ten feet by eight and five feet high. The foundation does not penetrate the deck, but the masonry is firmly secured to the surface by ponderous iron knees bracing it on all sides and screwing it down to the timbers. On the flanks it is encased with wood, and at the top completely covered by a large, sloping, battened hatchway. Removing this hatch, we expose the great try-pots, two in number, each of several barrels' capacity. When not in use, they are kept remarkably clean — sometimes polished with soapstone and sand till they shine within like silver punch-bowls. During night watches, some cynical old sailors will crawl into them and coil up for a nap. While polishing them — one man in each pot, side by side — many confidential conversations are carried on over the iron lips. It is a place also for deep mathematical meditation. It was in the left-hand try-pot of the Pequod, with the soapstone diligently circling round me, that I was first indirectly struck by the remarkable fact that in geometry all bodies sliding along a cycloid, my soapstone for example, will descend from any point in precisely the same time.

items.reason: Softened period language (lead decision 1 / hard rule 4): source "as their uncivilized laughter forked upwards out of them" became "their wild laughter". Also "scornfully champed the white bone in her mouth" became "bit", losing the champing (chewing at a bit) image.
items.new: The hatch, removed from the top of the works, now provided a wide hearth in front of them. Standing on this were the Tartarean shapes of the pagan harpooners, always the whale-ship's stokers. With huge pronged poles they pitched hissing masses of blubber into the scalding pots, or stirred up the fires beneath, till the snaky flames darted curling out of the doors to catch them by the feet. The smoke rolled away in sullen heaps. With every pitch of the ship there was a pitch of the boiling oil, which seemed all eagerness to leap into their faces. Opposite the mouth of the works, on the far side of the wide wooden hearth, was the windlass. This served as a sea-sofa. Here lounged the watch, when not otherwise employed, staring into the red heat of the fire till their eyes felt scorched in their heads. Their tawny features, now all grimed with smoke and sweat, their matted beards, and the contrasting barbaric brilliance of their teeth — all these were strangely revealed in the capricious flare of the works. As they told each other their unholy adventures, their tales of terror told in words of mirth — as their uncivilized laughter forked upward out of them, like flames from the furnace — as the harpooners wildly gesticulated in front of them with their huge pronged forks and dippers — as the wind howled on and the sea leaped and the ship groaned and dove and yet steadily shot her red hell further and further into the blackness of the sea and the night, and scornfully champed the white bone in her mouth and viciously spat round her on all sides — then the rushing Pequod, freighted with savages and laden with fire and burning a corpse and plunging into that blackness of darkness, seemed the material counterpart of her monomaniac commander's soul.

items.new: But that night in particular, a strange and ever since inexplicable thing occurred to me. Starting from a brief standing sleep, I was horribly conscious that something was fatally wrong. The jawbone tiller struck my side, which was leaning against it. In my ears was the low hum of sails just beginning to shake in the wind. I thought my eyes were open. I was half conscious of putting my fingers to the lids and mechanically stretching them still further apart. But despite all this, I could see no compass before me to steer by, though it seemed but a minute since I had been watching the card by the steady binnacle lamp. Nothing seemed before me but a jet-black gloom, now and then made ghastly by flashes of redness. Uppermost was the impression that whatever swift, rushing thing I stood on was not so much bound to any haven ahead as rushing from all havens astern. A stark, bewildered feeling, as of death, came over me. Convulsively my hands grasped the tiller, but with the crazy notion that the tiller was somehow, in some enchanted way, inverted. My God! What is the matter with me? I thought. Lo! In my brief sleep I had turned myself about, and was facing the ship's stern, with my back to the prow and the compass. In an instant I turned to face forward again, just in time to prevent the vessel from flying up into the wind and very probably capsizing her. How glad and how grateful the relief from this unnatural hallucination of the night, and the fatal danger of being brought by the lee!

items.new: But even Solomon, he says, "the man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain" — that is, even while living — "in the congregation of the dead." Do not give yourself up, then, to fire, lest it invert you, deaden you — as for the time it did me. There is a wisdom that is woe. But there is a woe that is madness. And there is a Catskill eagle in some souls that can alike dive down into the blackest gorges and soar out of them again and become invisible in the sunny spaces. And even if he forever flies within the gorge, that gorge is in the mountains; so that even in his lowest swoop the mountain eagle is still higher than other birds upon the plain, even though they soar.

items.new: It so happened that the doubloon of the Pequod was a most splendid example of these things. On its round border it bore the letters: REPUBLICA DEL ECUADOR: QUITO. So this bright coin came from a country planted in the middle of the world, beneath the great equator and named after it, and had been cast midway up the Andes in the unwaning climate that knows no autumn. Bordered by those letters, you saw the likeness of three Andean summits: from one a flame, a tower on another, on the third a crowing cock, while arching over all was a segment of the partitioned zodiac, the signs all marked with their usual mystic symbols, and the keystone sun entering the equinoctial point at Libra.

items.new: "No fairy fingers can have pressed the gold, but devil's claws must have left their markings there since yesterday," murmured Starbuck to himself, leaning against the bulwarks. "The old man seems to read Belshazzar's awful writing. I have never closely studied the coin. He goes below; let me read. A dark valley between three mighty, heaven-abiding peaks that almost seem the Trinity, in some faint earthly symbol. So in this vale of Death, God girds us round; and over all our gloom, the sun of Righteousness still shines as beacon and hope. If we bend down our eyes, the dark vale shows her moldy soil; but if we lift them, the bright sun meets our gaze halfway to cheer. Yet, oh, the great sun is no fixture; and if at midnight we would gladly snatch some sweet comfort from him, we look for him in vain! This coin speaks wisely, mildly, truly, but still sadly to me. I will leave it, lest Truth shake me falsely."

items.new: In less than a minute, without quitting his little craft, he and his crew were dropped to the water and were soon alongside the stranger. But here a curious difficulty arose. In the excitement of the moment, Ahab had forgotten that since the loss of his leg he had never once stepped aboard any vessel at sea but his own, and then it was always by an ingenious and very handy mechanical device peculiar to the Pequod — not a thing to be rigged and shipped in any other vessel at a moment's notice. Now it is no very easy matter for anybody — except those who are almost hourly used to it, like whalemen — to clamber up a ship's side from a boat on the open sea; for the great swells now lift the boat high up toward the bulwarks, and then instantly drop it halfway down to the keelson. So, deprived of one leg and the strange ship of course being altogether without the kindly invention, Ahab now found himself abjectly reduced to a clumsy landsman again, hopelessly eyeing the uncertain, changeful height he could hardly hope to reach.

items.new: At the time, I devoted three days to the studious digesting of all this beer, beef, and bread, during which many profound thoughts were incidentally suggested to me, capable of a transcendental and Platonic application. Furthermore, I compiled supplementary tables of my own, touching the probable quantity of stock-fish, etc., consumed by every Low Dutch harpooner in that ancient Greenland and Spitsbergen whale fishery. In the first place, the amount of butter and Texel and Leyden cheese consumed seems amazing. I attribute it, though, to their naturally oily natures, being rendered still more oily by the nature of their work, and especially by their pursuing their prey in those frigid polar seas, on the very coasts of that Eskimo country where the sociable natives toast each other in bumpers of whale-oil.
